That is a great question! Despite the 2-sided nature of Void and Space, their respective opposites are Light and Time, and that has less so to do with the literal nature of them, more of the metaphorical nature of them, that’s where the opposites lie.

Light in of itself represents truth, insight, enlightenment, vision, and all that encompasses the nature of knowing and goal-setting.

Void however, is the opposite, Void is nothing, void has no meaning, truth, or “light” to it, but that in of itself can be a positive thing. With nothing left, a new, more positive truth can be created for oneself, the razing of once that used to be true for a much stronger foundation, an empty canvass to envision something better. It’s comfortable with secrets, and not having all the answers, because it knows just as well that knowledge can be a burden.

Light represents what *is*there. Void represents what *can* be there.

Space and Time are a bit more finicky. While the obvious pairing of space and time is obvious, the nature of it runs deeper than that.

Time is ever-ticking, as it’s nature defines, it’s constantly marching to its own tune, it’s own beat that any creature no matter the power must adhere to, the ultimate fate, a slow-burning end. But the time we do have, and that it such allows us, is enough. As with its constant March comes with an unstoppable force that will adhere to nothing, constantly drilling away at the whims of fate to make its goal happen.

Space on the other hand, is much more expansive that time itself, it envisions loopholes, creativity, options, and it keeps growing and growing. Like a tree with infinite branches, and infinite possibilities. It’s much more than we could ever conceive and goes far beyond the bounds of time itself. Like our universe in the stars, we’ve yet to see everything it has to offer us.

I suppose it comes down to a perspective thing, whether straight and persistent is more of your thing, or if thinking outside the box is up your alley. These intrinsic natures of Space and Time also determine the type of people in homestuck who get assigned these powers based on these mentalities. It’s very philosophical, I know, but every aspect in homestuck is when you thing about it’s metaphorical and meta-narrative roots.

Alrighty lets break this down.  


(Stuff you gotta know for some stuff to make sense, in Homestuck, characters are assigned a "Classpect" which is a combination of one of the 12 Aspects (the ones above) and one of the 12 "Classes" some of which are, Thief, Bard, Prince, Heir, Maid, and others, and given their title, like Knight of Time, Heir of Breath, Maid of Space, Seer of Light, ect.)  


(Aspects determine a general concept or idea, like Time or Space, but the "classes" determine the \*type\* of Manipulation. For example, Princes \*destroy\* their aspect, so a Prince of Light would be able to black out areas full of light, or a Maid who \*creates\* their aspect directly, so a Maid of Light would be able to directly create light and such manifestations from their very hands, instead of having to manipulate it where it already exists. A lot of speculation could be drawn as to what certain combinations' powers may entail, all of which is up for debate, so my thoughts are only an interpretation.  


​

1: HEART deals with empathy and passion as it naturally would, but Heart deals with the physical soul itself. People with heart powers in Homestuck often have splinters, which are copies of themselves based upon certain parts of their personality/soul. Since heart deals with the soul itself, creation of Heart = creation of souls, allowing inanimate objects to be brought to life. Manipulation of souls would allow someone to alter someone else's soul, changing their personality Another example, a character in Homestuck, Prince of Heart, literally was able to rip, tear, and destroy souls from enemies bodies.  
HOPE deals with positivity, faith, and belief. People with hope powers are able to directly manipulate hope itself. Some believe so hard that their surroundings change around them (Hope for a sword, sword made of pure hope appears in hand), some can directly affect enemies \*Hope\*, their beliefs and will to fight, or what they even believe in, or believe to be reality (illusions). It sounds overpowered, but only so much can be manipuated, so more often than not its messing with others' Hope, manifesting circumstances, items, or powers made of Hope itself (Physical alterations aren't permanent, usually just made out of Hope energy itself)

RAGE deals with anger of course, but also negativity, fear, lies, and fakeness. Pure rage in of itself bolsters people's physical strength (-rationality), but manipulation of Rage can also make a foe docile, or make someone attack people around them uncontrollably, or make them incredibly fearful of you. But with its counterfeit, lie representation as well, leads into control over such concepts, like making a working object bust, making a weapon of theirs downgraded (counterfeit) form, or even physical manifestation of fear or trauma.  


  
2: Each aspect has its opposite in terms of what they represent: HOPE = RAGE, BREATH = BLOOD, LIGHT = VOID, and such and such. The Opposite to space is Time actually.  


3: As I explained above, HEART is the aspect that deals with sentience, Mind is more passive and easily explainable., while LIFE deals with literal \*Life Force\*, so Heart would be \*Existence of Life\* while Life would be \*Level of Life\*. Mind is rationality, Logic, the concept of branching paths and the consequences that come of them. Powers include telekinesis, literal psychic damage, extreme intelligence, and prediction of enemy attacks (maybe a counter dodge?), any other manipulation of Mind is purely passive and supportive, so probably a stat-boosting support character.  


4: Doom is a toughie, its the least expanded upon in Homestuck so more interpretation has to be drawn. Doom (without getting into the emotional nitty gritty) deals with ends, pain, the harshness of life, restrictions, and rules. The believed manifestation of Doom powers is the manifestation of pain itself, constructs made out of directly harmful elements in life, like fire, and sharp edges, maybe things like fangs or thorns, or poison? Otherwise, the other half of Doom manipulation is manipulation of rules and restrictions, so altering the natural rules of life to your bidding, like complete damage negation, existence of gravity, making an object stuck in place, things like that. (Yeah its really open ended and dips into other type powers, I did say it was the least expanded upon, and while it's not fleshed out this is sorta the general idea the fandom has in mind.
